options.content: **Simulated test data** (4 runs × 3 h, 12 injected faults), replayed from the AquaTwin pipeline on GitHub. Blue lines are sensor readings; dashed gray lines are the digital twin's expected values. The alarm uses the residual z-score chart (alarm when the score stays above 1 for 15 of 20 seconds). After a turbidity slug or an aeration failure the alarm can stay on 30–60 min, because the water stays abnormal until the filter and aeration bring it back to what the twin expects.

panels.description: What the simulator actually injected. Not available on real data; shown here to check the detector.

panels.description: Residual z-score chart, as a multiple of the alarm threshold.

panels.title: Anomaly score (× alarm threshold)
panels.description: 1.0 (dashed red line) is each detector's alarm threshold, set so a normal calibration run stays below it 99.5% of the time. Log scale.
